questions.prompt: A service gets 10 million requests per day, spread evenly. Roughly what is the average QPS?
questions.explanation: A day has 86,400 seconds, and 10,000,000 / 86,400 is about 116. Peak traffic is often several times the average, so design for the peak.

questions.prompt: What makes a poor shard key?
options: A low-cardinality or skewed key (e.g. country, or a timestamp for append-heavy writes) that creates hot shards
A key used in most queries
questions.explanation: Good keys spread load and match access patterns so most queries hit a single shard.

questions.prompt: Why use consistent hashing instead of hash(key) % N to assign keys to cache nodes?
options: Adding or removing a node remaps only about 1/N of the keys instead of nearly all of them
questions.explanation: With modulo, changing N reshuffles almost every key and empties the cache. Virtual nodes improve the balance of consistent hashing.

questions.prompt: What does a CDN primarily improve?
options: Latency and origin load for static or cacheable content, by serving it from edge locations near users
questions.explanation: Cache keys, TTLs and invalidation still need design.

questions.prompt: Why should list items in React have stable, unique keys (not array indexes when the order can change)?
options: React uses keys to match elements between renders; unstable keys can cause wrong state reuse and unnecessary re-mounts
questions.explanation: If items are reordered or inserted, index keys make React attach one item's state, such as input values, to another item.

questions.prompt: Which practice prevents most XSS in a React app?
options: Rendering user content as text (React escapes it by default) and avoiding raw HTML injection unless it is sanitised
questions.explanation: Also avoid javascript: URLs in links built from user input. A Content-Security-Policy adds defence in depth.

questions.prompt: What does CORS actually control?
options: Whether a server accepts requests at all
Whether the browser lets JavaScript from one origin read responses from another origin
questions.explanation: CORS is enforced by browsers, not servers. It is not authentication, and server-side authorization is still required.

questions.prompt: What does the STAR method stand for?
questions.explanation: Spend most of the time on your own Actions, and quantify the Result where you can.

questions.prompt: In a behavioral answer about a team project, what do interviewers want to hear?
options: Your specific contribution and decisions ("I"), while acknowledging the team
questions.explanation: Interviewers are assessing you. Be clear about which decisions and actions were yours.

questions.prompt: For "Tell me about a time you failed", what makes a strong answer?
options: A real failure you owned, what you did to recover, and what you changed afterwards
A failure caused entirely by others
questions.explanation: The signal is ownership and learning. A concrete process change you made afterwards makes the answer credible.

questions.prompt: What is Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)?
options: Retrieving relevant documents at query time and including them in the model's context so answers can be grounded in that data
questions.explanation: RAG keeps knowledge updatable without retraining. Retrieval quality is often the main factor in answer quality.

questions.prompt: What is a text embedding?
options: A compressed copy of the text
A dense vector where semantically similar texts are close under a similarity measure such as cosine similarity
questions.explanation: Vector search finds nearest neighbours, usually with approximate indexes such as HNSW for speed.

questions.prompt: Why does chunk size matter in RAG?
options: Chunks that are too large dilute relevance and waste context; chunks that are too small lose surrounding meaning
questions.explanation: Overlap, structure-aware splitting (headings, code blocks), and hybrid keyword plus vector search with re-ranking are common improvements.

questions.prompt: Why combine keyword search (e.g. BM25) with vector search?
options: Exact terms such as error codes, IDs and rare names are handled well by keyword search, while vectors capture paraphrases
questions.explanation: Results are often merged with reciprocal rank fusion, then re-ranked.

questions.prompt: In LLM tool calling, who actually executes the tool?
options: The application: the model outputs a structured request (tool name and arguments), the app runs it and returns the result
questions.explanation: Because the app executes the call, it must validate arguments and enforce permissions, just as it would for any untrusted input.

questions.prompt: What is the Model Context Protocol (MCP)?
options: An open protocol for connecting AI applications to external tools and data sources through standardised servers
questions.explanation: MCP servers expose tools, resources and prompts. Clients (AI apps) connect to them instead of building a custom integration for each one.

questions.prompt: What is indirect prompt injection?
options: A user typing a long prompt
Malicious instructions hidden in content the model reads (web pages, documents, tool results) that try to make it act against the user or system
questions.explanation: Mitigations include treating retrieved content as untrusted data, least-privilege tools, confirmations for risky actions, and output filtering.

questions.prompt: What is a sound basis for evaluating an LLM feature before shipping a change?
options: Trying a few prompts by hand
A fixed evaluation set of representative inputs with defined pass criteria, run on every change to catch regressions
Asking the model if it's correct
questions.explanation: Combine automated checks (exact match, schema validation, graders) with human review on samples, and track the results over time.

questions.prompt: Where should PII redaction happen when sending user data to an external model provider?
options: Before the data leaves your system, with detection plus policy (mask, tokenise, or block) and audit logging
questions.explanation: TLS protects data in transit, but the provider still receives the plaintext. Minimise what you send in the first place.

questions.prompt: What is LLM routing?
options: Choosing which model handles a request (e.g. a cheaper model for simple tasks, a stronger one for hard tasks) based on rules or a classifier
questions.explanation: The goal is to balance cost, latency and quality. Routers need evaluation too, because a misroute degrades quality silently.
